qualification_limits: Legacy compensation covers caught Python failures under cooperating local ownership; it is not crash-atomic across lattice, RAG, DPM/DCN, runtime KV or external projections.

Abrupt process death can leave split legacy components; this limitation is explicitly tested. Atomic receipt durability comes from the separate authoritative SQLite transaction and existing retry semantics.

Failed compensation remains a visible degraded outcome and may interrupt later component compensation; no durable recovery log, automatic poisoned-state policy or guaranteed complete repair is introduced.
Ordinary file refresh remains stat based. Content fingerprints protect failed write reconciliation, add prior-file read cost, and do not qualify arbitrary noncooperating file writers.
The PID guard protects inherited coordinator entry; it is not general fork-safety qualification of the adapter, providers or runtime.

The 256-client result has at most 32 active workers and does not qualify complete HTTP/provider cancellation, fairness, starvation, lock-latency, multi-host, network-filesystem or power-loss guarantees.
This bounded accepted extraction does not promote repository maturity or complete the remaining production-release qualification milestones.
